conventions.convention: Realification preserves the underlying set and addition and restricts scalar multiplication along the canonical embedding of R into C.
A complex norm is finite real-valued and absolutely homogeneous for every complex scalar; a complex normed subspace carries the restricted ambient norm.
An ordered basis is a finite injective list whose image is an independent spanning subset; indexing starts at zero, and the empty list is an ordered basis exactly for the zero space.
The finite complex basis is supplied, not asserted to exist. Its real basis is interleaved as b_0, ib_0, …, b_(n−1), ib_(n−1), including n=0; no choice axiom is used.
The example uses coordinatewise operations on C² and the norm N(z_1,z_2)=|z_1|+|z_2|.

load_bearing.statement: Let (V,N) be a complex normed space and let W⊆V be a complex normed subspace with its restricted norm. Then W_R is a real normed subspace of V_R, and its norm metric is the restriction of the metric on V_R to W×W. If an ordered complex basis (b_j)_(j<n) of W is supplied, the interleaved list b_0, ib_0, …, b_(n−1), ib_(n−1) is an ordered real basis of W_R. The basis clause includes n=0.

Checking the coordinate-sum norm supplier's use of nonnegativity, definiteness, multiplicativity and subadditivity of modulus.
